ousia-mathematike.definition: The intermediate ontological realm of mathematical objects: unmoved and exact unlike sensibles, yet pluralized and extended unlike pure indivisible Forms.

metaxy.definition: The middle rank occupied by mathematical reality and dianoia between pure Intellect (nous) and sense-perception/opinion (aisthesis/doxa).

peras.definition: First cosmic principle (from Plato's Philebus) bestowing boundary, definite ratio, symmetry, and intelligible form upon mathematical figures; also geometric extremity.

apeiron.definition: Complementary cosmic principle supplying inexhaustible progression, continuous divisibility, multiplicity, and infinite extendibility in magnitude and number.

nous.definition: Supreme intuitive intelligence contemplating simple, partless, unextended archetypal Forms prior to discursive unfolding.

dianoia.definition: The specifically mathematical faculty of the soul, unfolding innate intelligible logoi step-by-step from principles to conclusions.

doxa.definition: Cognitive faculty directed toward mutable sensible things, lacking knowledge of Demonstrative Causes (aitiai).

phantasia.definition: Formative intellective-imaginative screen ('passive nous') onto which dianoia projects universal logoi as extended, divisible, yet exact geometric figures.

hyle-noete.definition: Aristotelian term reinterpreted by Proclus as the pure spatial extension in phantasia individualizing plural congruent circles and triangles; central to Hoenen's Caput IV.

probole.definition: The active projection by which dianoia unfolds its partless internal reason-principles onto the mirror-like screen of phantasia to examine their properties.

hysterogenes.definition: Concept formed empirically a posteriori from sense-objects; rejected by Proclus for mathematics because sensibles lack exactness and necessity.

anamnesis.definition: Platonic awakening of the soul's substantial mathematical logoi from within, illustrated by the Meno's doubling of the square.

stoicheion.definition: A foundational proposition whose mastery pervades and unlocks the demonstration of many subsequent theorems, as letters compose speech.

stoicheiosis.definition: Systematic deductive arrangement ascending from first principles through elementary propositions to the capstone of a science.

horos.definition: Both a conceptual definition delimiting an essence (Defs. 1–23) and the geometric boundary enclosing a figure (Def. 13).

hypothesis.definition: An unproved assumption posited by the teacher and conceded by the learner as the starting point of demonstration.

aitema.definition: A constructive geometric demand (Posts. 1–5) whose subject-matter is easy to contrive or grant without prior demonstration.

axioma.definition: An indemonstrable, self-evident truth common to multiple sciences (e.g. 'things equal to the same are equal to one another').

problema.definition: A proposition proposing the constructive generation, division, or placement of a geometric figure not yet brought to view (ending 'what it was required to do').

theorema.definition: A proposition demonstrating an essential attribute belonging per se to a given geometric figure (ending 'what it was required to prove').

protasis.definition: Universal statement declaring what is given and what is sought, prior to any lettered diagram.

ekthesis.definition: Instantiating the given of the enunciation in a concrete lettered figure in phantasia ('Let AB be the given finite straight line...').

diorismos.translation: specification / condition of possibility (3rd of 6 parts)
diorismos.english: specification / condition of possibility (3rd of 6 parts)
diorismos.definition: In theorems/problems, restating the sought goal on the set-out figure; in problems like I.22, also the necessary and sufficient condition for solvability.

kataskeue.definition: Auxiliary lines and circles drawn via postulates and earlier problems to prepare the figure for demonstration.

apodeixis.definition: Syllogistic deduction inferring the sought attribute or construction validity from first principles through essential causes (aitiai).

symperasma.definition: Re-ascending from the particular lettered diagram back to the universal truth of the enunciation, sealed by Q.E.F. or Q.E.D.

lemma.definition: A proposition assumed in a proof while requiring independent confirmation elsewhere.

ptosis.definition: Positional variation of a construction (e.g. point inside, on, or outside a figure) requiring distinct verification of the same theorem.

porisma.definition: Either (1) an incidental gain emerging unbidden from a demonstration (as I.15 Porism), or (2) finding an existing geometric entity intermediate between problem and theorem.

enstasis.definition: A counter-argument blocking either a geometric construction or a step of demonstration (e.g. Zeno of Sidon against I.1).

apagoge.definition: Transition from a harder problem or theorem to another whose solution immediately yields the proposed goal (e.g. Hippocrates on duplicating the cube).

adynaton.definition: Indirect proof assuming the contradictory of the sought conclusion to deduce the overthrow of a conceded axiom, hypothesis, or prior theorem.

analysis.definition: Upward path assuming the thing sought as granted and tracing consequences back to an admitted principle; transmitted by Plato to Leodamas.

synthesis.definition: Downward deductive path proceeding from admitted principles through intermediate steps to the conclusion.

antistrophe.definition: Interchanging hypothesis and conclusion between leading (proegoumenon) and converse (antistrophon) theorems, either completely or partially.

epharmoge.definition: Fitting one geometric magnitude onto another in imagination without physical distortion (CN 4, Prop. I.4, I.8).

rhysis.definition: Unextended motion of a point generating a line, or uniform undeviating flux generating a straight line (cited in Greek by Hoenen at p. 121).

homoiomeres.definition: A curve every part of which coincides with every other part: proved by Geminus to comprise solely the straight line, circle, and cylindrical helix.

keratoeides.definition: Curvilinear-rectilinear angle between a circle and its tangent, smaller than every acute rectilinear angle yet non-zero—challenging Archimedean magnitude.

gnomon.definition: Oenopides of Chios's archaic astronomical name for the perpendicular (Prop. I.12), drawn from the upright sundial pointer.

topikon-theorema.definition: Theorem invariant across an infinite locus of positions—inaugurated in the Elements by Prop. I.35 (equal parallelograms between parallel lines).

parabole.definition: Pythagorean construction applying a given area exactly along a given segment (Prop. I.44); transferred by Apollonius to the parabola.

hyperbole.definition: Applying an area along a line so as to overlap beyond its extremity by a similar figure; origin of the name of the hyperbola.

elleipsis.definition: Applying an area along a line so as to fall short of its extremity by a similar figure; origin of the name of the ellipse.
